title: Journal Club: Therapeutic Video Game on Trial

reader_summary.headline: Hello and welcome to the A16Z Journal Club, our podcast where we cover recent scientific advances in bio.
reader_summary.overview: Hello and welcome to the A16Z Journal Club, our podcast where we cover recent scientific advances in bio, why they matter. Today's episode covers the topic of digital therapeutics, given that earlier this month, the FDA approved its first ever prescription video game. And since this is a journal club, we go into one of the key clinical trials underpinning this historic decision, published recently in Lancet Digital Health.

key_points.text: Hello and welcome to the A16Z Journal Club, our podcast where we cover recent scientific advances in bio, why they matter.
key_points.evidence_quote: Hello and welcome to the A16Z Journal Club, our podcast where we cover recent scientific advances in bio, why they matter, and how to take them from proof of principle to practice.

key_points.text: And since this is a journal club, we go into one of the key clinical trials underpinning this historic decision.
key_points.evidence_quote: And since this is a journal club, we go into one of the key clinical trials underpinning this historic decision, published recently in Lancet Digital Health, by Scott Collins and colleagues, which evaluated this game's ability to improve attention in kids with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder or ADHD.

key_points.text: Our sister podcast, 16 minutes on the news, also covered this topic.
key_points.evidence_quote: Our sister podcast, 16 minutes on the news, also covered this topic, debating the bigger picture questions of what is and isn't a digital therapeutic and where pricing and regulation comes in.
